note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a BUR 6, 7; A06b BUR 6, 7; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 10 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Burundi, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident at least 10 years. ... n.a. ... n.a. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is the child of a citizen (constitution), or person is born in wedlock to a father who is a citizen, or is recognised by voluntary or court-ordered legitimation as the child of a Burundian father, or paternal descent is not established and the child is recognised voluntarily or by court order as the child of a Burundian mother, or the child is repudiated by the father and the mother is a citizen (law). ... Generally applicable provision ... Constitution: person is the child of a citizen. Law: person is born in wedlock to a father who is a citizen, or is recognised by voluntary or court-ordered legitimation as the child of a Burundian father, or paternal descent is not established and the child is recognised voluntarily or by court order as the child of a Burundian mother, or the child is repudiated by the father and the mother is a citizen. ...
